tier_reason: The nativejson-benchmark numbers were measured on snapshot 0d6259e, which reserved 16 slots in every array and object (explaining the 34.4 MB canada.json figure); that reservation was removed in 65df934 and the benchmark was never rerun, so the published numbers describe code that no longer exists (numbers-before-later-fix precedent). The library also has lookup bugs (find/at return the next key for a missing key) and a libstdc++ memcpy-move hazard outside the measured path.

corrections.caveats: Measured snapshot 0d6259e pre-allocated 16 slots per container (removed in 65df934, not rerun); built only with clang/libc++ (libstdc++ COW assumption breaks SSO strings); find/at return the next key for a missing key; no depth limit; numbers are double only.

tier_reason: Tier unchanged; caveats refreshed from code reading and a scratch spot check.

corrections.caveats: Pretty-print 9.3x/3.7x rows are a CPython 3.10 artefact (3.13 json.dumps(indent) uses the C encoder, about 1.72x on citm); first-party benchmark runs ujson ensure_ascii=False vs json default True and its UTF-8 rows decode pure \u escapes; orjson harness keeps json's spaced separators. ujson 6.0.0 on CPython 3.13 still leads 1.21x-3.31x on all 16 rows (scratch spot check, not tier evidence). Lenient loads ('-', '01', '1.', raw control chars), Decimal through float, __json__ spliced unvalidated, 1.4-1.75x retained memory. Int-key sort segfault and lone \ud800 handling fixed.

tier_reason: Not reproducible: the 2011 harness targets the C++03 GCallbackList that was rewritten in C++11 in 2017 and no longer compiles against current code (numbers-on-since-changed-code precedent); every cell is a single run quantised to the 15.625 ms Windows XP clock() tick, so the single-slot gaps against libsigc++ are 1-3 ticks of noise, and Boost.Signals2 ran with its default mutex against unlocked libraries.

corrections.caveats: 2011 table (VC 9 -O2, GCC 4.5.2 -O3, Pentium E2180) measured the pre-2017 C++03 GCallbackList; harness no longer compiles against current code. All 64 cells are multiples of the 15.625 ms clock() tick, one run each (single-slot gaps vs libsigc++ are noise); native rows are collapsed loops; Boost.Signals2 ran locked vs unlocked competitors; Boost single-slot rows time signals2::slot. Current code: operator() forwards the same arguments to every slot (moved-from values after the first), operator= overloads lack a return, member callbacks always heap-allocate. C++11 required since 1.6. Project discontinued; author points to eventpp.
